chunks.section: Item 4. Advisory Business > 4.1 Firm Overview
chunks.text: Sallowmere Capital Management, LP is a Delaware limited partnership formed in 2016 by Callum R. Everdeen, who serves as Managing Partner and Chief Investment Officer. The Adviser has been registered with the SEC as an investment adviser since March 2017. The general partner of the Adviser is Sallowmere Management Holdings LLC. Mr. Everdeen is the Adviser's principal owner and holds his interest through Sallowmere Management Holdings LLC. Mireille Dansby, President and Chief Operating Officer, holds a minority interest in Sallowmere Management Holdings LLC. As of December 31, 2025, the Adviser had 22 employees, of whom 10 are investment professionals: the Chief Investment Officer, seven sector analysts, the Head of Trading and one execution trader. The Adviser's Management Committee, composed of Mr. Everdeen, Ms. Dansby, Oren Pellisier (Chief Financial Officer) and Harriet Lomasney (General Counsel and Chief Compliance Officer), oversees the Adviser's business, operations and compliance program.

chunks.section: Item 4. Advisory Business > 4.2 The Funds
chunks.text: The Adviser provides discretionary investment advisory services to three private investment funds (each a "Fund" and together the "Funds"): - Sallowmere Partners Fund, LP (the "Flagship Fund"), a Delaware limited partnership that commenced trading on January 3, 2017 and pursues a fundamental long/short equity strategy. The Flagship Fund also serves as the master fund in a "mini-master" structure. - Sallowmere Partners Offshore Fund, Ltd. (the "Offshore Fund"), a Cayman Islands exempted company that commenced operations on July 2, 2018 and is registered with the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority under the Mutual Funds Act (As Revised). The Offshore Fund invests substantially all of its assets in the Flagship Fund as a limited partner and is offered principally to non-U.S. investors and to U.S. tax-exempt investors. - Sallowmere Co-Investment Fund I, LP (the "Co-Investment Fund"), a Delaware limited partnership formed in June 2024 to hold a concentrated position in the listed common stock of a single mid-capitalization industrial technology issuer (the "Co-Investment Issuer"), together with a privately negotiated senior unsecured convertible note issued by the Co-Investment Issuer (the "Convertible Note"). Interests in the Co-Investment Fund were offered only to existing investors in the Flagship Fund and the Offshore Fund. Sallowmere Partners GP, LLC serves as general partner of the Flagship Fund, and Sallowmere Co-Invest GP, LLC serves as general partner of the Co-Investment Fund (each a "General Partner"). Each General Partner is under common control with the Adviser. The Offshore Fund is governed by a board of directors, a majority of whom are independent of the Adviser. The Adviser acts as investment manager to each Fund under a written investment management agreement.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 4. Advisory Business > 4.3 Tailored Services and Investment Restrictions
chunks.text: The Adviser manages each Fund in accordance with the investment objective, guidelines and restrictions in its Offering Documents, and not according to the individual needs of any investor. Investors may not impose restrictions on investing in particular securities or types of securities. Side letters with certain investors grant enhanced transparency, notice or most-favored-nation rights or, in limited cases, reduced fees, but do not alter the investment program of any Fund. The Adviser does not participate in wrap fee programs.

chunks.section: Item 4. Advisory Business > 4.4 Assets Under Management
chunks.text: As of December 31, 2025, the Adviser managed regulatory assets under management of $1,874,612,000, all on a discretionary basis. The Adviser does not manage any assets on a non-discretionary basis. Regulatory assets under management are calculated on a gross basis as required by Form ADV, without deduction for short positions, margin borrowings or other liabilities, and without double counting the Offshore Fund's investment in the Flagship Fund. As of the same date, the net asset value of the Flagship Fund was approximately $1,182.4 million, including the Offshore Fund's investment of approximately $512.6 million, and the net asset value of the Co-Investment Fund was approximately $97.8 million.

chunks.section: Item 5. Fees and Compensation > 5.1 Management Fees
chunks.text: The Flagship Fund pays the Adviser a management fee at the following annual rates, which are also set out in the Adviser's Fee Schedule: - Class A interests: 2.00% per annum of each limited partner's capital account. - Class A interests of an investor whose aggregate capital in the Flagship Fund and the Offshore Fund, together with that of its affiliates, is $50 million or more as of the first day of a calendar quarter: 1.50% per annum on the investor's entire capital account (the "Large Investor Rate"). - Class F (founders') interests, closed to new investment since December 31, 2018: 1.25% per annum. - Class E interests, held only by the Adviser's principals and employees and their family members: no management fee. Management fees attributable to the Offshore Fund's investment in the Flagship Fund are charged once, at the Flagship Fund level, on a look-through basis by reference to the share class held by each Offshore Fund shareholder. The Offshore Fund does not pay a separate management fee.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 5. Fees and Compensation > 5.2 Billing
chunks.text: Management fees are calculated and payable quarterly in advance as of the first business day of each calendar quarter, based on each capital account (or, for the Offshore Fund, each shareholder's pro rata share of the Offshore Fund's capital account) as of that date, before accrual of any incentive allocation. The Flagship Fund and the Offshore Fund accept subscriptions monthly, and a subscription accepted as of a date other than the first day of a calendar quarter bears a management fee pro-rated for the balance of that quarter. Management fees are debited from Fund assets by the Administrator (as defined in Item 15).

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 5. Fees and Compensation > 5.3 Other Fees and Expenses
chunks.text: Each Fund bears its own operating expenses, including brokerage commissions, financing and stock borrow charges, interest, fees of the Administrator, audit, tax and legal fees, fees of the directors of the Offshore Fund, and research paid for with commissions as described in Item 12. The Adviser bears its own overhead, including compensation, rent, general office technology and the cost of alternative data and expert network services. Organizational expenses of the Co-Investment Fund were borne by that Fund up to a cap of $150,000, with any excess borne by the Adviser.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 5. Fees and Compensation > 5.4 Redemptions, Early Redemption Fee and Refunds
chunks.text: Limited partners of the Flagship Fund and shareholders of the Offshore Fund may redeem as of the last business day of any calendar quarter on at least 65 days' prior written notice. Redemptions effective within 12 months after an investor's initial subscription are subject to an early redemption fee of 3% of the amount redeemed, which is retained by the relevant Fund and not paid to the Adviser. A full redemption is subject to a holdback of 10% of the proceeds pending completion of the Fund's annual audit, and 90% of redemption proceeds are ordinarily paid within 30 days after the redemption date. Each of the Flagship Fund and the Offshore Fund may limit aggregate redemptions as of any quarter-end to 20% of its net asset value. If a General Partner permits a redemption as of a date other than a quarter-end, or if an investment management agreement terminates during a quarter, the unearned portion of the prepaid management fee is refunded pro rata. Each investment management agreement may be terminated by either party on 90 days' prior written notice.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 5. Fees and Compensation > 5.5 Co-Investment Fund
chunks.text: The Co-Investment Fund does not pay a management fee. Sallowmere Co-Invest GP, LLC receives carried interest as described in Item 6. Investors in the Co-Investment Fund have no right to redeem, and distributions are made upon the disposition of its investments. The term of the Co-Investment Fund ends on the earlier of the disposition of all of its investments and June 30, 2029, subject to two one-year extensions at the discretion of its General Partner.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 5. Fees and Compensation > 5.6 Negotiability of Fees
chunks.text: Fees are negotiable in the discretion of the relevant General Partner or the board of directors of the Offshore Fund. Certain investors pay reduced fees under side letters, and the fees described in this Item 5 are therefore not necessarily the fees paid by any particular investor.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 6. Performance-Based Fees and Side-by-Side Management > 6.1 Incentive Allocation
chunks.text: As of December 31 of each year, and as of the effective date of any redemption, Sallowmere Partners GP, LLC receives an incentive allocation from each Class A capital account in the Flagship Fund equal to 20% of the net profits allocated to that capital account for the period, and from each Class F capital account equal to 15% of such net profits. Class E capital accounts bear no incentive allocation. The incentive allocation is subject to a high water mark: no incentive allocation is made from a capital account until prior net losses allocated to it have been recovered. There is no hurdle rate. For the Offshore Fund's investment, the incentive allocation is calculated on a look-through basis and allocated once, at the Flagship Fund level.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 6. Performance-Based Fees and Side-by-Side Management > 6.2 Co-Investment Fund Carried Interest
chunks.text: Sallowmere Co-Invest GP, LLC is entitled to carried interest equal to 10% of the net realized profits of the Co-Investment Fund, distributed only after investors have received distributions equal to 100% of their capital contributions and their share of Co-Investment Fund expenses. No carried interest is paid on unrealized gains.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 6. Performance-Based Fees and Side-by-Side Management > 6.3 Qualified Clients
chunks.text: Performance-based compensation is charged only in accordance with Rule 205-3 under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 (the "Advisers Act"), and each investor in a Fund must be a "qualified client" as defined in that rule.

chunks.section: Item 6. Performance-Based Fees and Side-by-Side Management > 6.4 Side-by-Side Management and Conflicts of Interest
chunks.text: Performance-based compensation may create an incentive to make riskier or more speculative investments. Because the incentive allocation is calculated on realized and unrealized net profits, valuation directly affects the General Partner's compensation, a conflict addressed through the Valuation Policy described in Item 15. The Adviser manages the Flagship Fund and the Co-Investment Fund side by side. The Flagship Fund pays a management fee and an annual incentive allocation, while the Co-Investment Fund pays no management fee and a lower carried interest on realized profits only. This difference may create an incentive to favor the Flagship Fund in allocating purchases and sales of securities of the Co-Investment Issuer. The Adviser mitigates this conflict through the allocation priority rule described in Item 12 and through review by the Chief Compliance Officer of every allocation in securities of the Co-Investment Issuer.

chunks.section: Item 7. Types of Clients > 7.1 Clients and Investor Eligibility
chunks.text: The Adviser's clients are the three Funds described in Item 4. Investors include high net worth individuals, family offices, endowments, foundations, pension plans and funds of funds. Interests are offered in private placements exempt from registration under the Securities Act of 1933. Each investor must be an "accredited investor" under Regulation D and a "qualified purchaser" under Section 2(a)(51) of the Investment Company Act of 1940, and each Fund relies on the exclusion in Section 3(c)(7) of that Act. Each of the Flagship Fund and the Offshore Fund limits investment by "benefit plan investors" to less than 25% of the value of each class of equity interests, so that its assets are not deemed "plan assets" subject to Title I of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974. Interests may not be transferred without consent.

chunks.text: The minimum initial investment in each of the Flagship Fund and the Offshore Fund is $1,000,000, and the minimum additional investment is $250,000. The minimum commitment to the Co-Investment Fund was $5,000,000. Each General Partner, and the board of directors of the Offshore Fund, may accept lesser amounts in its discretion.

chunks.section: Item 8. Methods of Analysis, Investment Strategies and Risk of Loss > 8.1 Methods of Analysis
chunks.text: The Adviser employs fundamental, bottom-up research. Sector analysts cover mid- and large-capitalization companies in the industrials, consumer and technology hardware sectors, principally in North America and Western Europe. Research includes public filings, proprietary earnings models, management meetings, channel checks, expert network consultations and licensed alternative data. Short positions are established on specific theses, such as deteriorating unit economics or accounting quality concerns, and as hedges of sector or factor exposure. The Chief Investment Officer makes all final investment decisions.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 8. Methods of Analysis, Investment Strategies and Risk of Loss > 8.2 Investment Strategy and Portfolio Guidelines
chunks.text: The Flagship Fund seeks attractive risk-adjusted returns with lower volatility than the broad equity market by holding long positions in companies the Adviser believes are undervalued and short positions in companies it believes are overvalued. The Flagship Fund invests principally in listed equity securities and also uses total return swaps, listed options, exchange-traded funds, and currency forwards to hedge non-U.S. dollar exposure. The Flagship Fund operates under the following portfolio guidelines, each measured against its net asset value: - Gross exposure may not exceed 250% of net asset value, and has typically ranged between 160% and 220%. - Net exposure must remain between negative 10% and positive 80% of net asset value, and has typically ranged between 25% and 55%. - No single long position may exceed 8% of the Flagship Fund's net asset value, measured at market value. - No single short position may exceed 4% of the Flagship Fund's net asset value, measured at market value. The Co-Investment Fund was formed because the Adviser's desired position in the Co-Investment Issuer exceeded the Flagship Fund's single long position guideline and because the Convertible Note is illiquid. The Co-Investment Fund is not subject to the Flagship Fund's guidelines and is expected to remain concentrated in a single issuer for its entire term.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 8. Methods of Analysis, Investment Strategies and Risk of Loss > 8.3 Risk Management
chunks.text: The Head of Risk, Ingrid Vallancey, reports to the Chief Operating Officer and is independent of the investment team. The risk function produces daily exposure, liquidity and stress scenario reports and monitors the portfolio guidelines in Item 8.2 before and after trading through the order management system. A breach of any portfolio guideline is reported to the Chief Investment Officer and the Chief Compliance Officer on the day it is identified.

chunks.section: Item 8. Methods of Analysis, Investment Strategies and Risk of Loss > 8.4 Material Risks
chunks.text: **Illiquidity and valuation risk.** The Convertible Note is not listed and may be sold only in privately negotiated transactions, if at all. Its value is determined using a model and unobservable inputs under the Valuation Policy and may differ materially from the price at which it could be sold. The valuation of the Convertible Note does not affect carried interest until the note is sold or converted, but it does affect reported net asset value. **Reliance on the Chief Investment Officer.** The success of the Funds depends substantially on the judgment of Mr. Everdeen, and his death, disability or departure could adversely affect the Funds and prompt redemptions. **Operational and cybersecurity risk.** The Adviser and its service providers rely on information systems that may be disrupted or compromised by cyber attacks, system failures or natural disasters. The Adviser's business continuity plan and information security program do not eliminate these risks. **Redemption and liquidity risk.** Significant redemptions could require the Flagship Fund to liquidate positions at unfavorable prices and increase the concentration and leverage of the remaining portfolio. **Regulatory, tax and currency risk.** Changes in securities or tax laws may adversely affect the Funds or the Adviser, and investments in Western European issuers are subject to currency risk that hedges may not fully offset.

chunks.section: Item 11. Code of Ethics, Participation or Interest in Client Transactions and Personal Trading > 11.1 Code of Ethics
chunks.text: The Adviser has adopted a Code of Ethics under Rule 204A-1 under the Advisers Act. The Code of Ethics sets standards of business conduct, requires compliance with federal securities laws, requires all employees (each of whom is treated as an access person) to report personal securities holdings and transactions, and requires prompt internal reporting of violations. The Adviser will provide a copy of the Code of Ethics to any investor or prospective investor on request.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 11. Code of Ethics, Participation or Interest in Client Transactions and Personal Trading > 11.2 Personal Trading
chunks.text: Employees may trade for their own accounts in securities that the Funds also buy, sell or hold, which creates a conflict of interest. To address this conflict, employees must obtain pre-clearance from the Compliance department before any transaction in a reportable security and may not trade in any security on the Adviser's restricted list. Employees may not trade in a security within seven calendar days before or after a Fund trades in that security, and must hold any position for at least 30 calendar days. Employees may not participate in initial public offerings, and investments in private placements require the prior written approval of the Chief Compliance Officer. Employees may not hold short positions in any security held long by the Flagship Fund.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 11. Code of Ethics, Participation or Interest in Client Transactions and Personal Trading > 11.3 Principal and Cross Transactions
chunks.text: The Adviser does not engage in principal transactions with the Funds and does not effect cross trades between the Funds.

chunks.section: Item 11. Code of Ethics, Participation or Interest in Client Transactions and Personal Trading > 11.4 Investment by Principals and Employees in the Funds
chunks.text: The Adviser's principals and employees invest in the Flagship Fund through Class E interests, which bear no management fee or incentive allocation. These investments may create an incentive to favor the Flagship Fund over the Co-Investment Fund, in which personnel do not invest.

chunks.section: Item 12. Brokerage Practices > 12.1 Selection of Executing Brokers
chunks.text: The Adviser has discretion to select brokers and dealers to execute Fund transactions and to negotiate commission rates. The Adviser seeks best execution, meaning the most favorable overall terms reasonably available under the circumstances, and does not necessarily select the broker offering the lowest commission. Factors considered include execution price, commission rates, handling of large or difficult orders, confidentiality, financial stability, settlement reliability and research. In 2025 the Adviser engaged Tessingham Execution Analytics LLC to provide independent transaction cost analysis, which the Adviser's Best Execution Committee reviews.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 12. Brokerage Practices > 12.2 Prime Brokers
chunks.text: Brisworth Tallent Securities LLC serves as the primary prime broker to the Flagship Fund and the Co-Investment Fund, and Quarrington Prime Services LLC serves as a second prime broker to the Flagship Fund. The prime brokers provide custody, clearing, margin financing and securities lending, and affiliates of each serve as swap counterparties. The Adviser reviews prime broker financing rates, borrow availability and credit standing at least annually.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 12. Brokerage Practices > 12.3 Research and Other Soft Dollar Benefits
chunks.text: The Adviser receives research products and services from brokers in connection with Fund brokerage, including through commission sharing arrangements with a limited number of executing brokers under which a portion of the commissions paid on Fund transactions is credited to a pool that the Adviser directs to pay independent research providers. Research obtained includes written research, industry data and market data services. The Adviser pays the non-research portion of any mixed-use product from its own resources. The Adviser intends that all such arrangements fall within the safe harbor of Section 28(e) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. Research obtained with Fund commissions may be used in managing all of the Funds, not only the Fund whose transactions generated the commissions. Because the Adviser does not pay for research obtained with commissions, it has an incentive to select brokers based on its interest in receiving research, and the Funds may pay commissions higher than those charged by other brokers. The Best Execution Committee reviews the commission budget semi-annually through a broker vote.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 12. Brokerage Practices > 12.4 Brokerage for Client Referrals and Directed Brokerage
chunks.text: The Adviser does not select brokers in consideration of investor referrals. The capital introduction group of Brisworth Tallent Securities LLC has from time to time introduced prospective investors to the Adviser without compensation, and the Adviser does not consider such introductions in allocating brokerage. The Adviser does not permit investors to direct brokerage.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 12. Brokerage Practices > 12.5 Aggregation and Allocation of Orders
chunks.text: The Adviser may aggregate orders for more than one Fund when it believes aggregation is consistent with best execution. Each aggregated order is pre-allocated in the order management system before it is placed, all participating Funds receive the average price, and partially filled orders are allocated pro rata in proportion to the pre-allocation. Purchases of securities of the Co-Investment Issuer are allocated between the Flagship Fund and the Co-Investment Fund in accordance with the priority rule in the Adviser's allocation policy, which is designed so that the Co-Investment Fund holds only the portion of the position that the Flagship Fund cannot hold consistent with its portfolio guidelines. Employee orders are never aggregated with Fund orders.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 12. Brokerage Practices > 12.6 Trade Errors
chunks.text: If a trade error occurs as a result of the Adviser's negligence or a breach of a Fund's guidelines, the Adviser reimburses the Fund for any resulting loss. Gains resulting from a trade error are retained by the Fund. The Chief Compliance Officer maintains a log of all trade errors and their resolution.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 13. Review of Accounts > 13.1 Periodic Reviews
chunks.text: The Chief Investment Officer reviews each Fund's portfolio daily. The Head of Risk reviews daily exposure, liquidity and stress scenario reports and chairs a weekly risk meeting with the Chief Investment Officer and the Head of Trading. The Chief Financial Officer reviews each Fund's net asset value and fee calculations monthly.

chunks.section: Item 13. Review of Accounts > 13.2 Reports to Investors
chunks.text: The Administrator delivers a monthly capital account statement (or, for the Offshore Fund, a monthly statement of shareholding and net asset value per share) to each investor in the Flagship Fund and the Offshore Fund within fifteen business days after each month-end. The Head of Investor Relations, Celia Brandvold, distributes an estimated monthly performance figure within five business days after each month-end and a quarterly investor letter, including exposure and attribution data, within 45 days after each quarter-end. Investors in the Co-Investment Fund receive quarterly capital account statements from the Administrator. All investors receive annual audited financial statements as described in Item 15 and tax information as soon as practicable after year-end.

chunks.text: The Adviser has engaged Wexcombe Partners Ltd., a London-based placement agent, to introduce non-U.S. institutional investors to the Offshore Fund in the United Kingdom and Switzerland. The placement agreement was renewed in 2025 for a further three-year term. Wexcombe Partners Ltd. receives 20% of the management fees and incentive compensation received by the Adviser and the General Partner that are attributable to investors it introduces, for as long as those investors remain invested. These fees are paid by the Adviser from its own resources and are not charged to the Offshore Fund or its shareholders. This compensation gives the placement agent an incentive to recommend the Offshore Fund.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 14. Client Referrals and Other Compensation > 14.2 Other Compensation
chunks.text: The Adviser does not receive any economic benefit, other than the research described in Item 12, from any person other than the Funds for providing advisory services to the Funds.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 15. Custody > 15.1 Custody and Audited Financial Statements
chunks.text: The Adviser is deemed to have custody of Fund assets because its affiliates serve as general partners of the Flagship Fund and the Co-Investment Fund and because the Adviser has authority to withdraw Fund assets. The Adviser complies with Rule 206(4)-2 under the Advisers Act by having each Fund audited annually by Brennock Lyle LLP, an independent public accountant registered with, and subject to regular inspection by, the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board, and by distributing audited financial statements prepared in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles to all investors within 120 days after the end of each fiscal year. Each Fund's fiscal year ends on December 31. Fund cash and securities are held by the prime brokers as qualified custodians. The Convertible Note is a privately offered security recorded in the name of the Co-Investment Fund on the register maintained by the Co-Investment Issuer.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 15. Custody > 15.2 Administrator
chunks.text: Carvell Brink Fund Services Ltd. (the "Administrator") serves as administrator to each of the Funds. The Administrator maintains the Funds' books and records, independently calculates net asset value, processes subscriptions and redemptions, performs investor anti-money laundering and sanctions screening, and delivers investor statements. Investors should carefully review the statements they receive from the Administrator.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 15. Custody > 15.3 Valuation
chunks.text: The Adviser values Fund assets under a written Valuation Policy adopted by the Management Committee. Valuation determinations are made by a Valuation Committee chaired by the Chief Financial Officer, whose voting members do not include the Chief Investment Officer or any member of the investment team. Listed securities are valued using prices from independent pricing vendors, and the Convertible Note is valued using a model reviewed by an independent valuation firm.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 16. Investment Discretion > 16.1 Discretionary Authority
chunks.text: The Adviser has discretionary authority under each investment management agreement and the Offering Documents to determine the securities to be bought and sold for each Fund, the amounts of those securities, the brokers used and the commissions paid, without obtaining investor consent. This authority is limited by the portfolio guidelines described in Item 8.2, the Offering Documents and applicable law.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026
chunks.section: Item 17. Voting Client Securities > 17.1 Proxy Voting Policy
chunks.text: The Adviser has adopted proxy voting policies and procedures under Rule 206(4)-6 under the Advisers Act. The Adviser has engaged Harlaxton Proxy Services LLC to provide proxy research, vote execution and recordkeeping. The analyst responsible for an issuer recommends each vote, and the Chief Investment Officer approves it. The Adviser may abstain where the cost of voting, such as share blocking or the recall of loaned securities, exceeds the expected benefit. If the Chief Compliance Officer determines that the Adviser has a material conflict of interest with respect to a vote, the Adviser votes in accordance with the standard policy recommendation of Harlaxton Proxy Services LLC. Investors may not direct votes, and may obtain the Adviser's proxy voting policies and a record of votes cast on request.

chunks.label: Form ADV Part 2A: Firm Brochure, dated March 27, 2026

chunks.text: The Adviser does not require or solicit prepayment of more than $1,200 in fees per client six months or more in advance, and therefore is not required to include a balance sheet with this brochure. The Adviser is not aware of any financial condition that is reasonably likely to impair its ability to meet its contractual commitments to the Funds, and has not been the subject of a bankruptcy petition at any time during the past ten years.

chunks.section: Preamble
chunks.text: # Compliance Manual **Sallowmere Capital Management, LP** Version date: January 15, 2026 > **SYNTHETIC DOCUMENT: FOR BENCHMARK USE ONLY.** This document is fictional. Sallowmere Capital Management, LP, Sallowmere Partners Fund, LP, Sallowmere Partners Offshore Fund, Ltd., Sallowmere Co-Investment Fund I, LP and all persons, service providers and figures named herein are invented for the purpose of evaluating document-processing systems. It is not an offer to sell securities and does not describe any real entity.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. INTRODUCTION > 1.1 Purpose and Scope
chunks.text: This Compliance Manual (the "Manual") sets out the written policies and procedures that Sallowmere Capital Management, LP (the "Adviser") has adopted under Rule 206(4)-7 under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 (the "Advisers Act") to prevent, detect and correct violations of the federal securities laws. The Manual applies to the Adviser, to Sallowmere Partners GP, LLC and Sallowmere Co-Invest GP, LLC (the "General Partners"), and to the management of Sallowmere Partners Fund, LP (the "Flagship Fund"), Sallowmere Partners Offshore Fund, Ltd. (the "Offshore Fund") and Sallowmere Co-Investment Fund I, LP (the "Co-Investment Fund" and, together with the Flagship Fund and the Offshore Fund, the "Funds"). The Valuation Policy and the Business Continuity Plan are separate documents adopted under this Manual.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. INTRODUCTION > 1.2 Supervised Persons
chunks.text: Every partner, officer and employee of the Adviser, and any other person who provides advice on behalf of the Adviser and is subject to its supervision and control, is a "supervised person." Each supervised person must read the Manual, comply with it, and acknowledge it in writing on hire, annually and upon any material amendment. Temporary staff and consultants are subject to the provisions the Chief Compliance Officer designates in writing.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. INTRODUCTION > 1.3 Amendments and Interpretation
chunks.text: Amendments to the Manual, the Valuation Policy, the Business Continuity Plan and the Fee Schedule are approved by the Management Committee, composed of the Managing Partner, the President and Chief Operating Officer, the Chief Financial Officer and the General Counsel and Chief Compliance Officer. Between full revisions, approved amendments are issued by written memorandum of the Chief Compliance Officer, which identifies the provision amended and supersedes it from the stated effective date. Questions of interpretation are resolved by the Chief Compliance Officer, whose determination is final. Where the Manual is silent, supervised persons must act in accordance with the Adviser's fiduciary duty to the Funds.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. CHIEF COMPLIANCE OFFICER > 2.1 Designation
chunks.text: The Management Committee has designated Harriet Lomasney, General Counsel, as Chief Compliance Officer ("CCO"). Ms. Lomasney has served in that role since 2019. The CCO is responsible for administering this Manual and has the authority to develop and enforce appropriate policies and procedures.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. CHIEF COMPLIANCE OFFICER > 2.2 Reporting Line and Authority
chunks.text: The CCO reports to Callum R. Everdeen, Managing Partner and Chief Investment Officer, and has direct access to the Management Committee and to the board of directors of the Offshore Fund. The CCO has unrestricted access to all books, records, systems and personnel of the Adviser, may retain outside counsel and consultants at the Adviser's expense, and may escalate any matter directly to the full Management Committee without prior notice to any other person. No supervised person may retaliate against the CCO or any member of the Compliance department for the good faith performance of compliance duties.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. CHIEF COMPLIANCE OFFICER > 2.3 Deputy Chief Compliance Officer
chunks.text: Desmond Achterberg serves as Deputy Chief Compliance Officer ("Deputy CCO"). The Deputy CCO acts for the CCO in the CCO's absence, administers the personal trading program and electronic communications surveillance day to day, and maintains the compliance calendar.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. CHIEF COMPLIANCE OFFICER > 2.4 Compliance Calendar and Recordkeeping
chunks.text: The Compliance department maintains a calendar of recurring obligations, including Form ADV annual amendments, Form 13F and Schedule 13G filings, Form PF filings, blue sky and non-U.S. private placement notices, Offshore Fund filings with the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority, and the internal reviews described in this Manual. Completion of each item is documented in the compliance platform.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. CODE OF ETHICS > 3.1 Standards of Business Conduct
chunks.text: This Section 3 and Section 4 together constitute the Adviser's Code of Ethics under Rule 204A-1 under the Advisers Act. Supervised persons must act with honesty, integrity and care; place the interests of the Funds and their investors ahead of their own; avoid actual and potential conflicts of interest or disclose them to the CCO; comply with applicable federal securities laws; and safeguard confidential information about Fund holdings and trading.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. CODE OF ETHICS > 3.2 Access Persons and Covered Accounts
chunks.text: All employees of the Adviser are designated access persons. A "covered account" is any account in which an access person has direct or indirect beneficial ownership, including accounts of a spouse, domestic partner, minor child or other household member, and any account over which the access person exercises investment discretion. Accounts managed by an unaffiliated third party over which the access person has no influence or control may be exempted by the CCO in writing on receipt of a certification from the access person and the manager.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. CODE OF ETHICS > 3.3 Reporting Violations
chunks.text: Supervised persons must report any actual or suspected violation of this Manual promptly to the CCO or, if the matter involves the CCO, to the Managing Partner. Reports may be made anonymously through the compliance platform. The Adviser does not retaliate against any person for a good faith report.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. CODE OF ETHICS > 3.4 Sanctions
chunks.text: Violations may result in a warning, disgorgement of profits, reversal of trades at the supervised person's expense, suspension of personal trading privileges, a reduction in discretionary compensation, or termination of employment. The CCO reports material violations to the Management Committee.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. CODE OF ETHICS > 3.5 Outside Business Activities
chunks.text: Supervised persons may not engage in any outside business activity, including service as an officer, director, general partner, adviser or consultant to any other business, without the prior written approval of the CCO. Service as a director of a public company is prohibited. Unpaid service with a charitable or civic organization requires notice to the CCO, and approval where the organization is an investor or prospective investor in a Fund.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PERSONAL TRADING > 4.1 Reportable Securities and Exemptions
chunks.text: All securities are reportable securities except direct obligations of the U.S. government, bankers' acceptances, bank certificates of deposit, commercial paper, high quality short-term debt instruments, money market fund shares, and shares of open-end mutual funds. Exchange-traded funds, closed-end funds, options, single-stock futures, cryptocurrency-linked exchange-traded products and private placements are reportable.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PERSONAL TRADING > 4.2 Pre-Clearance
chunks.text: Access persons must obtain pre-clearance before any transaction in a reportable security in a covered account, other than transactions in the broad-based index exchange-traded funds on the list maintained by the Compliance department and transactions under an automatic investment plan. Requests are submitted through the compliance platform and are approved or denied by the CCO or the Deputy CCO. Pre-clearance requests submitted by the CCO are approved by the President and Chief Operating Officer, Mireille Dansby. Approval is valid only for the business day on which it is granted; an order not executed by the close of regular trading that day requires a new request. Limit orders that remain open beyond that day are not permitted. Compliance may deny any request without stating a reason.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PERSONAL TRADING > 4.3 Blackout Periods and Restricted List
chunks.text: An access person may not trade in a security within seven calendar days before or after a Fund trades in that security or in a derivative referencing it, and may not trade while a Fund order in that security is pending. Access persons may not trade in any security on the Restricted List described in Section 7.2. The CCO will review any trade executed during a blackout period and may require it to be reversed with any profit disgorged.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PERSONAL TRADING > 4.4 Prohibited Transactions
chunks.text: Access persons may not acquire securities in an initial public offering. Investments in private placements require the prior written approval of the CCO, which considers whether the opportunity should be offered to a Fund. Access persons may not sell short, or buy put options on, any security held long by the Flagship Fund, and may not engage in any transaction designed to profit from, or that front-runs, a Fund trade.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PERSONAL TRADING > 4.5 Minimum Holding Period
chunks.text: Access persons must hold any position in a reportable security acquired in a covered account for at least 30 calendar days from the date of acquisition before disposing of it, and may not close a short position within 30 calendar days of opening it. Profits realized on a transaction that violates this Section 4.5 are disgorged to a charity selected by the CCO. The CCO may grant a written hardship exception, including where a security is sold at a loss.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PERSONAL TRADING > 4.6 Holdings and Transaction Reports
chunks.text: Each access person must submit an initial holdings report within 10 calendar days after becoming an access person, with information current as of a date not more than 45 days before the person became an access person. Each access person must submit a quarterly transaction report within 30 calendar days after the end of each calendar quarter, and an annual holdings report by February 14 of each year with information current as of December 31 of the prior year. Access persons must arrange for each broker holding a covered account to provide duplicate statements or an electronic data feed to the Compliance department, which satisfies the report content requirements where it contains the required information.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. PERSONAL TRADING > 4.7 Review of Personal Trading
chunks.text: The Deputy CCO reviews all holdings and transaction reports and compares personal trades against Fund trading, pre-clearance records, the Restricted List and blackout periods. The CCO's reports and trades are reviewed by the President and Chief Operating Officer. Exceptions are documented and reported to the CCO.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. GIFTS AND ENTERTAINMENT > 5.1 General Principles
chunks.text: Supervised persons may not give or accept any gift or entertainment that could reasonably be expected to influence a business decision, including the selection of brokers, counterparties, vendors or service providers, or an investor's decision to invest in a Fund. Cash and cash equivalents may never be given or accepted.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. GIFTS AND ENTERTAINMENT > 5.2 Gifts Received
chunks.text: Supervised persons may accept gifts from any person or entity that does business or seeks to do business with the Adviser or the Funds, including brokers and research providers, with an aggregate value not exceeding $250 per source per calendar year. Gifts in excess of that limit must be declined or surrendered to the Compliance department.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. GIFTS AND ENTERTAINMENT > 5.3 Gifts Given
chunks.text: Supervised persons may give gifts to any person associated with a current or prospective investor, service provider or counterparty with an aggregate value not exceeding $250 per recipient per calendar year. All gifts given are paid for by the Adviser and never by a Fund.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. GIFTS AND ENTERTAINMENT > 5.4 Business Entertainment
chunks.text: Business entertainment, such as meals and sporting or cultural events, is permitted only where the host attends and the entertainment is neither lavish nor frequent. Entertainment with a value exceeding $500 per person per event requires the prior approval of the CCO. Travel and lodging provided by a broker or vendor may not be accepted without CCO approval and is ordinarily paid for by the Adviser.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. GIFTS AND ENTERTAINMENT > 5.5 Government Officials, Union Officials and Plan Fiduciaries
chunks.text: No gift or entertainment may be given to a government official, including an official or employee of a public pension plan, without the prior approval of the CCO, who will consider applicable federal, state and local gift and ethics rules and Section 6. Gifts and entertainment provided to officials of labor unions are subject to Department of Labor reporting on Form LM-10, and gifts to fiduciaries of ERISA plans are limited to amounts permissible under Department of Labor guidance.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. GIFTS AND ENTERTAINMENT > 5.6 Recording and Reporting
chunks.text: Supervised persons must record in the compliance platform, within five business days, every gift and every item of entertainment given or received, other than promotional items of nominal value under $50. The Deputy CCO reviews the log monthly, and the Best Execution Committee receives a summary of gifts and entertainment received from brokers at each meeting.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. POLITICAL CONTRIBUTIONS > 6.1 Scope
chunks.text: The Adviser has adopted this Section 6 under Rule 206(4)-5 under the Advisers Act. One or more government entities, including public pension plans, are investors in the Flagship Fund. A contribution by a covered associate to an official of a government entity could prohibit the Adviser from receiving compensation from that government entity for two years.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. POLITICAL CONTRIBUTIONS > 6.2 Pre-Clearance and Limits
chunks.text: All supervised persons, whether or not covered associates, must obtain the prior written approval of the CCO before making any political contribution to a candidate for or holder of federal, state or local office, a political party, or a political action committee, and before engaging in any fundraising activity. The CCO will approve contributions by covered associates only within the following limits: up to $350 per election to an official for whom the covered associate is entitled to vote, and up to $150 per election to an official for whom the covered associate is not entitled to vote. Contributions by a spouse or household member that are directed or funded by a supervised person are treated as contributions of the supervised person.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. POLITICAL CONTRIBUTIONS > 6.3 New Covered Associates
chunks.text: Before an offer of employment is made to any person who would be a covered associate, the Compliance department reviews that person's political contributions for the preceding two years, or six months for a person who will not solicit investors. The CCO must approve the hire if any contribution during that period exceeded the limits in Section 6.2.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. POLITICAL CONTRIBUTIONS > 6.4 Solicitation, Bundling and Payments to Third Parties
chunks.text: Supervised persons may not solicit or coordinate contributions to an official of a government entity to which the Adviser provides or seeks to provide advisory services, or to a political party of the state or locality of that entity. The Adviser does not pay any third party to solicit government entities unless the third party is a regulated person under Rule 206(4)-5 and the arrangement is approved by the CCO.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. INSIDER TRADING AND MATERIAL NONPUBLIC INFORMATION > 7.1 Policy
chunks.text: Supervised persons may not trade, for a Fund or any covered account, while in possession of material nonpublic information ("MNPI") about an issuer or its securities, and may not communicate MNPI to any other person except as permitted by this Section 7. Information is material if a reasonable investor would consider it important in making an investment decision, and nonpublic if it has not been disseminated in a manner making it available to investors generally.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. INSIDER TRADING AND MATERIAL NONPUBLIC INFORMATION > 7.2 Restricted List and Watch List
chunks.text: The CCO maintains a Restricted List of issuers in which no trading for the Funds or covered accounts is permitted, and a confidential Watch List of issuers about which the Adviser may possess sensitive information. Restrictions are coded in the order management system to block Fund orders. Issuers are removed from the Restricted List only by the CCO, after confirming that the information has become public or is no longer material.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. INSIDER TRADING AND MATERIAL NONPUBLIC INFORMATION > 7.3 Wall-Crossings
chunks.text: Only the Chief Investment Officer or the CCO may consent to receive MNPI in connection with a proposed offering or transaction. When an issuer or its agent requests a wall-crossing, the recipient must decline to receive any further detail and refer the request to the CCO. On consent, the issuer is placed on the Restricted List immediately and remains there until cleansing disclosure is made.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. INSIDER TRADING AND MATERIAL NONPUBLIC INFORMATION > 7.4 Expert Networks
chunks.text: Supervised persons may use only expert network firms approved by the CCO after due diligence on the firm's compliance procedures. Each consultation must be scheduled through the approved network's platform and pre-approved by the Compliance department. The Adviser does not consult current employees of any public company or of any government agency, or any person subject to a duty of confidentiality regarding the topic of the call. Each call opens with a reminder that the expert may not disclose MNPI or confidential information. The Compliance department chaperones the first call with each new expert and at least 10% of all subsequent calls, selected at random. Analysts must retain notes of every call in the research management system.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. INSIDER TRADING AND MATERIAL NONPUBLIC INFORMATION > 7.5 Alternative Data
chunks.text: Alternative data sets may be licensed only after the Compliance department and the Director of Technology complete due diligence on the vendor, including the source of the data, whether it was obtained in breach of any contractual or legal restriction, and whether it contains personal information.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. INSIDER TRADING AND MATERIAL NONPUBLIC INFORMATION > 7.6 Procedures on Receipt of MNPI
chunks.text: A supervised person who believes he or she may have received MNPI must stop trading in the issuer for all accounts, refrain from communicating the information to anyone other than the CCO, and report the matter to the CCO immediately. The CCO determines whether to add the issuer to the Restricted List and documents the determination.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. MARKETING AND INVESTOR COMMUNICATIONS > 8.1 Review and Approval
chunks.text: All advertisements within the meaning of Rule 206(4)-1 under the Advisers Act, including pitch books, tear sheets, investor letters, website content and presentations to prospective investors, must be approved in writing by the CCO before first use. Material changes to approved materials require re-approval. The Compliance department retains each approved version with its supporting documentation.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. MARKETING AND INVESTOR COMMUNICATIONS > 8.2 Performance Presentation
chunks.text: Performance is presented net of all fees and expenses, and gross performance is shown only alongside net performance calculated over the same period and with equal prominence. Performance of the Flagship Fund is presented for one-, five- and ten-year periods, or since inception where shorter. Extracted, hypothetical and predecessor performance may not be used without the specific written approval of the CCO and the policies and procedures Rule 206(4)-1 requires. The Adviser does not use testimonials. Its only endorsements are the compensated solicitation activities of the placement agent described in Section 8.4, which are conducted under a written agreement and subject to the disclosure and oversight conditions of Rule 206(4)-1.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. MARKETING AND INVESTOR COMMUNICATIONS > 8.3 Due Diligence Questionnaires and Requests for Proposal
chunks.text: Responses to due diligence questionnaires and requests for proposal are drafted by Investor Relations, reviewed for accuracy by the relevant function head, and approved by the CCO before release. Standard responses are refreshed at least annually and whenever an underlying policy changes.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. MARKETING AND INVESTOR COMMUNICATIONS > 8.4 Placement Agent Oversight
chunks.text: Wexcombe Partners Ltd. may use only materials approved under Section 8.1 and must provide the CCO with a quarterly certification of compliance with its placement agreement. The CCO reviews the placement agent's regulatory status annually.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 9. TRADE ALLOCATION AND AGGREGATION > 9.1 Aggregation
chunks.text: Orders for more than one Fund in the same security may be aggregated where the Head of Trading believes aggregation is consistent with best execution. Orders for covered accounts are never aggregated with Fund orders.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 9. TRADE ALLOCATION AND AGGREGATION > 9.2 Pre-Allocation
chunks.text: Before an aggregated order is placed, the portfolio management team records the intended allocation to each Fund in the order management system. Each participating Fund receives the average execution price and bears its pro rata share of commissions.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 9. TRADE ALLOCATION AND AGGREGATION > 9.3 Partial Fills and Deviations
chunks.text: Partially filled orders are allocated pro rata in proportion to the pre-allocation, subject to rounding to round lots. Any allocation that deviates from the pre-allocation must be approved by the CCO before the end of the trade date, with the reason documented.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 9. TRADE ALLOCATION AND AGGREGATION > 9.4 Co-Investment Issuer Allocations
chunks.text: Purchases of securities of the Co-Investment Issuer are allocated first to the Flagship Fund until the Flagship Fund's position reaches the single long position limit in its portfolio guidelines, and the balance of the order is allocated to the Co-Investment Fund. Sales of securities of the Co-Investment Issuer are allocated pro rata in proportion to each Fund's holdings immediately before the sale, unless the CCO approves a different allocation in writing to restore the Flagship Fund's compliance with its guidelines. The CCO reviews every allocation in securities of the Co-Investment Issuer on the trade date.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 9. TRADE ALLOCATION AND AGGREGATION > 9.5 Trade Errors
chunks.text: A trade error is any error in the placement, execution, allocation or settlement of a Fund trade, including a trade that breaches a Fund guideline. Errors must be reported to the Head of Trading and the CCO on discovery and corrected promptly. The Adviser reimburses a Fund for any loss resulting from an error caused by the Adviser's negligence or a guideline breach, and any gain is retained by the Fund. Errors resulting in a loss of more than $10,000 are reported to the Management Committee. The CCO maintains the trade error log.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 10. BEST EXECUTION > 10.1 Duty
chunks.text: The Adviser seeks to obtain the most favorable overall terms reasonably available for each Fund transaction, considering price, commission, speed and likelihood of execution, market impact, confidentiality, counterparty credit and the value of research.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 10. BEST EXECUTION > 10.2 Best Execution Committee
chunks.text: The Best Execution Committee consists of the President and Chief Operating Officer (chair), the Head of Trading, the Chief Financial Officer and the CCO. The Committee meets quarterly and reviews independent transaction cost analysis prepared by Tessingham Execution Analytics LLC, commission rates and totals by broker, execution quality exceptions, the soft dollar budget and gifts and entertainment received from brokers. Minutes are kept by the Compliance department.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 10. BEST EXECUTION > 10.3 Approved Brokers
chunks.text: Fund orders may be placed only with brokers on the approved broker list. A new broker requires the approval of the Best Execution Committee following review of its financial condition, regulatory history and operational capabilities, and each broker's standing is reviewed at least annually.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 10. BEST EXECUTION > 10.4 Commission Sharing Arrangements
chunks.text: Research credits under commission sharing arrangements are used only for research products and services that qualify for the safe harbor of Section 28(e) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. The Best Execution Committee approves the research budget semi-annually following a broker vote in which the investment team rates the research and execution of each broker. Mixed-use products are allocated in writing by the Chief Financial Officer, and the non-research portion is paid by the Adviser.

chunks.label: Compliance Manual, dated January 15, 2026

chunks.section: Preamble
chunks.text: # Valuation Policy and Procedures **Sallowmere Capital Management, LP** Version date: November 3, 2025 > **SYNTHETIC DOCUMENT: FOR BENCHMARK USE ONLY.** This document is fictional. Sallowmere Capital Management, LP, Sallowmere Partners Fund, LP, Sallowmere Partners Offshore Fund, Ltd., Sallowmere Co-Investment Fund I, LP and all persons, service providers and figures named herein are invented for the purpose of evaluating document-processing systems. It is not an offer to sell securities and does not describe any real entity.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated November 3, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 1. PURPOSE, SCOPE AND PRINCIPLES > 1.1 Purpose
chunks.text: This Valuation Policy and Procedures (the "Policy") governs the valuation of all investments held by Sallowmere Partners Fund, LP (the "Flagship Fund"), Sallowmere Partners Offshore Fund, Ltd. (the "Offshore Fund") and Sallowmere Co-Investment Fund I, LP (the "Co-Investment Fund" and, together, the "Funds"), each managed by Sallowmere Capital Management, LP (the "Adviser"). The Policy was adopted by the Management Committee and is administered by the Valuation Committee. Because the Adviser's management fee and the incentive allocation and carried interest received by its affiliates depend on the value of Fund assets, the Policy is designed to ensure that valuations are fair, consistently applied, independent of the investment team and fully documented.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated November 3, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 1. PURPOSE, SCOPE AND PRINCIPLES > 1.2 Scope and Frequency
chunks.text: The Policy applies to the monthly net asset value of each Fund calculated by Carvell Brink Fund Services Ltd. (the "Administrator"), to the Adviser's daily estimated net asset values used for risk management and investor estimates, and to the fair value measurements reported in each Fund's annual audited financial statements.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated November 3, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 1. PURPOSE, SCOPE AND PRINCIPLES > 1.3 Fair Value Standard
chunks.text: Investments are valued at fair value as defined in Accounting Standards Codification Topic 820, meaning the price that would be received to sell an asset, or paid to transfer a liability, in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. Each investment is classified in the fair value hierarchy as Level 1 (unadjusted quoted prices in active markets for identical instruments), Level 2 (observable inputs other than Level 1 prices) or Level 3 (significant unobservable inputs). Classification is proposed by the Controller and approved by the Valuation Committee.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated November 3, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 2. VALUATION COMMITTEE > 2.1 Composition
chunks.text: The Valuation Committee (the "Committee") has four voting members: the Chief Financial Officer, Oren Pellisier, who chairs the Committee; the President and Chief Operating Officer, Mireille Dansby; the Head of Risk, Ingrid Vallancey; and the Controller, Lydia Marchbanks, who also acts as secretary. The General Counsel and Chief Compliance Officer attends every meeting as a non-voting member. The Chief Investment Officer and members of the investment team may attend to provide information about an investment, but may not vote and are excused before any vote is taken.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated November 3, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 2. VALUATION COMMITTEE > 2.2 Quorum and Voting
chunks.text: A quorum consists of three voting members, one of whom must be the Chief Financial Officer or the Chief Operating Officer. Determinations are made by majority vote of the voting members present. A member with a personal interest in a determination must disclose it and abstain. Determinations may be made by unanimous written consent of all voting members when a meeting cannot be convened in time.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated November 3, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 2. VALUATION COMMITTEE > 2.3 Meetings
chunks.text: The Committee meets quarterly, within ten business days after the end of each calendar quarter, and on an ad hoc basis whenever the Chief Financial Officer, the Chief Operating Officer or the Chief Compliance Officer determines that a valuation matter requires prompt determination, including a trading halt, a suspension, a corporate event or a significant market dislocation affecting a Fund holding.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated November 3, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 2. VALUATION COMMITTEE > 2.4 Responsibilities
chunks.text: The Committee approves pricing sources and methodologies; approves the fair value hierarchy classification of each investment; determines the fair value of each Level 3 investment and of any investment for which a reliable market price is unavailable; reviews price challenges, overrides, stale price reports, tolerance exceptions and back-testing results; reviews the work of the independent valuation firm; and recommends amendments to this Policy to the Management Committee. The secretary records minutes of every meeting, including the materials reviewed and the basis for each determination.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated November 3, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 3. PRICING HIERARCHY AND SOURCES > 3.1 Primary and Secondary Pricing Vendors
chunks.text: The Committee has approved Orrisdale Market Data LLC as the primary pricing vendor and Pennick Pricing Services Inc. as the secondary pricing vendor. The Administrator obtains prices directly from the approved vendors under its own agreements, and the Controller receives the same feeds for the Adviser's daily estimates. A change in an approved vendor requires Committee approval.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated November 3, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 3. PRICING HIERARCHY AND SOURCES > 3.2 Listed Equities and Exchange-Traded Funds
chunks.text: Equity securities and exchange-traded funds listed on a securities exchange are valued at the official closing price on the primary exchange as reported by the primary pricing vendor. If no trade occurred on the valuation date, long positions are valued at the closing bid price and short positions at the closing ask price. Non-U.S. equities are converted into U.S. dollars at the 4:00 p.m. London closing rate supplied by the primary pricing vendor.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated November 3, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 3. PRICING HIERARCHY AND SOURCES > 3.3 Listed Options
chunks.text: Listed options are valued at the mean of the closing bid and ask prices on the exchange with the greatest volume. Where the spread exceeds 20% of the mean, the Controller refers the position to the Chief Financial Officer, who may approve use of the last traded price or a model price.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated November 3, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 3. PRICING HIERARCHY AND SOURCES > 3.4 Total Return Swaps
chunks.text: Total return swaps on single equities and baskets are valued using the closing price of the underlying securities determined under Section 3.2, adjusted for accrued financing and dividends. The Controller reconciles each swap valuation daily to the counterparty statement, and differences exceeding 0.10% of notional are investigated and resolved with the counterparty.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated November 3, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 3. PRICING HIERARCHY AND SOURCES > 3.5 Currency Forwards and Cash
chunks.text: Currency forwards are valued using forward points and spot rates supplied by the secondary pricing vendor, interpolated to the settlement date. Cash, margin balances and money market fund shares are valued at their reported balances or net asset value.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated November 3, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 3. PRICING HIERARCHY AND SOURCES > 3.6 Vendor Tolerance Checks
chunks.text: Each business day the Controller compares the prices supplied by the primary and secondary pricing vendors for every position. Differences exceeding 1% for equities and exchange-traded funds, or 2% for over-the-counter derivatives, are investigated and resolved before the daily estimate is released, and any unresolved difference is reported to the Chief Financial Officer. The Controller also investigates any daily price change of more than 15% for a single position that is not explained by public news.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated November 3, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 4. LEVEL 3 METHODOLOGY > 4.1 Scope
chunks.text: Level 3 investments currently consist of the senior unsecured convertible note held by the Co-Investment Fund (the "Convertible Note") and issued by the single listed issuer whose common stock the Co-Investment Fund also holds (the "Co-Investment Issuer"), together with any security that becomes subject to a prolonged trading suspension or for which the Committee determines that no reliable market price exists.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated November 3, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 4. LEVEL 3 METHODOLOGY > 4.2 Convertible Note Model
chunks.text: The Convertible Note is valued using a binomial lattice model that values the note as a combination of a straight debt instrument and an embedded option to convert into the Co-Investment Issuer's common stock, and that reflects the issuer's call right and the holder's put right under the note indenture. The model is calibrated at inception so that the model value equals the transaction price, and the calibrated inputs are carried forward and updated at each valuation date.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated November 3, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 4. LEVEL 3 METHODOLOGY > 4.3 Unobservable Inputs
chunks.text: The significant unobservable input is the credit spread applied to the straight debt component, which is determined by reference to the calibrated spread at inception, adjusted for changes in the spreads of comparable issuers' senior unsecured debt and for issuer-specific developments such as changes in leverage and liquidity. Volatility is derived from 180-day historical volatility of the Co-Investment Issuer's common stock, cross-checked against implied volatility on listed options where available. The Controller prepares a sensitivity analysis showing the effect of a 100 basis point change in credit spread and a five-point change in volatility.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated November 3, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 4. LEVEL 3 METHODOLOGY > 4.4 Documentation
chunks.text: For each Level 3 valuation the Controller prepares a valuation memorandum setting out the methodology, each input and its source, changes since the prior valuation, and the sensitivity analysis. The memorandum is approved by the Committee and provided to the independent valuation firm, the Administrator and the auditor.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated November 3, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 5. PRICE CHALLENGES AND OVERRIDES > 5.1 Price Challenges
chunks.text: If the Head of Trading, the Controller or the Chief Financial Officer believes that a vendor price does not reflect fair value, the Controller submits a written challenge to the vendor with supporting evidence, such as executed trades, broker quotes or corporate event information. While a challenge is pending, the vendor price continues to be used unless an override is approved under Section 5.2. The Controller maintains a log of every challenge and its outcome.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated November 3, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 5. PRICE CHALLENGES AND OVERRIDES > 5.2 Overrides
chunks.text: Any override of a vendor price, broker quote or model value used by the Administrator requires the written approval of the Chief Financial Officer and one other voting member of the Committee. The request must state the reason for the override, the proposed price, its source and the effect on net asset value. The Chief Investment Officer and members of the investment team may not approve an override. The Controller notifies the Administrator of each approved override on the day of approval.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated November 3, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 5. PRICE CHALLENGES AND OVERRIDES > 5.3 Reporting
chunks.text: All challenges and overrides since the prior meeting are reported to the full Committee, together with the subsequent market price of each overridden position where available.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated November 3, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 6. STALE PRICE MONITORING > 6.1 Stale Price Reports
chunks.text: The Administrator and the Controller each produce a daily report of positions whose price has not changed. A price that is unchanged for three consecutive business days is flagged and investigated by the Controller. A price that is unchanged for five consecutive business days is escalated to the Chief Financial Officer. A price that is unchanged for ten consecutive business days may not continue to be used without a fair value determination by the Committee. Positions subject to a trading halt are escalated immediately.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated November 3, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 7. BACK-TESTING > 7.1 Back-Testing Procedures
chunks.text: Each quarter the Controller compares the value assigned to each Level 3 investment, and to each position that was valued by override or fair value determination, with the price realized on any subsequent sale or the first subsequent observable market price. Differences exceeding 5% are documented with an explanation and reported to the Committee, which considers whether the methodology or inputs should be changed. The results of back-testing are also provided to the independent valuation firm.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated November 3, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 8. INDEPENDENT REVIEW AND OVERSIGHT > 8.1 Independent Valuation Firm
chunks.text: Kilbride Sayer Valuation Advisors LLC performs a quarterly review of each Level 3 investment and provides a written range of reasonable values. If the value approved by the Committee falls outside that range, the Chief Financial Officer must convene the Committee to reconsider the value before the Administrator finalizes the quarter-end net asset value, and the Chief Compliance Officer must be notified of the outcome.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated November 3, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 8. INDEPENDENT REVIEW AND OVERSIGHT > 8.2 Administrator
chunks.text: The Administrator independently obtains prices for all Level 1 and Level 2 positions, calculates each Fund's net asset value, and reports to the Controller every position for which its price differs from the Adviser's price. The Administrator applies Level 3 values approved by the Committee and receives the supporting valuation memorandum.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated November 3, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 8. INDEPENDENT REVIEW AND OVERSIGHT > 8.3 Auditor
chunks.text: Brennock Lyle LLP, the Funds' independent auditor, examines the Funds' valuations as part of its annual audit. The Controller provides the auditor with the Committee's minutes, all Level 3 valuation memoranda and the reports of the independent valuation firm.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated November 3, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 8. INDEPENDENT REVIEW AND OVERSIGHT > 8.4 Conflicts of Interest
chunks.text: No person whose compensation is determined by the performance of a particular position may approve its value. The Chief Compliance Officer reviews the Committee's minutes and the override log each quarter for indications of bias and reports any concern to the Management Committee.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated November 3, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 9. RECORDKEEPING AND POLICY REVIEW > 9.1 Records
chunks.text: All pricing data, challenge and override records, stale price reports, Level 3 valuation memoranda, back-testing results and Committee minutes are retained in accordance with Section 13 of the Compliance Manual.

chunks.label: Valuation Policy and Procedures, dated November 3, 2025
chunks.section: SECTION 9. RECORDKEEPING AND POLICY REVIEW > 9.2 Policy Review
chunks.text: The Committee reviews this Policy at least annually and recommends any amendments to the Management Committee. The Chief Compliance Officer reviews the Policy as part of the annual compliance review.
