chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated February 9, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. CRITICAL VENDORS > 5.3 Vendor Continuity Review
chunks.text: As part of the annual vendor due diligence described in Section 11.4 of the Compliance Manual, the BCP Coordinator obtains and reviews each critical vendor's business continuity summary and most recent independent control report, confirms its recovery commitments are consistent with the tiers in Section 4.1, and documents any gap and the Adviser's mitigation.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated February 9, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. DATA BACKUP AND RECOVERY > 6.1 Backup Frequency
chunks.text: The Adviser's file storage, email and portfolio accounting data are backed up through a third-party immutable backup platform administered by the IT managed service provider. Hourly incremental snapshots are taken during each business day, and a full backup is taken nightly at 11:00 p.m. Eastern Time. The order management system and market data are hosted by their vendors, whose backup arrangements are reviewed under Section 5.3.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated February 9, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. DATA BACKUP AND RECOVERY > 6.2 Storage Locations and Retention
chunks.text: Backup copies are encrypted in transit and at rest and are stored in two geographically separate data centers in Ashburn, Virginia and Columbus, Ohio, neither of which is located within 100 miles of the Adviser's office. Daily backups are retained for 35 days, and month-end backups are retained for seven years consistent with Section 13.2 of the Compliance Manual. Backup copies are immutable and cannot be altered or deleted by any Adviser or vendor account during the retention period.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated February 9, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. DATA BACKUP AND RECOVERY > 6.3 Restore Verification
chunks.text: The IT managed service provider restores a sample of files, mailboxes and the portfolio accounting database from backup each quarter and reports the results, including restore times, to the BCP Coordinator.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated February 9, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. TESTING > 7.1 Frequency
chunks.text: The Plan is tested through a full exercise at least annually, including relocation of the designated personnel to the alternate site for a full trading day and restoration of Tier 1 and Tier 2 systems, and through a call tree exercise every six months. The BCP Coordinator also conducts an annual tabletop exercise of the cyber incident response procedures in Section 9.2 with the Incident Response Team.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated February 9, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 7. TESTING > 7.2 Most Recent Exercises
chunks.text: The most recent full exercise was conducted on November 14, 2025. Six employees operated from the Norwalk alternate site for the full trading day, the remaining employees worked remotely, and all Tier 1 systems were available within the four-hour RTO. The exercise identified a delay in activating the recorded softphone licenses, which was remediated in December 2025. The most recent call tree exercise was conducted on January 22, 2026. Results of each exercise are reported in writing to the Management Committee.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated February 9, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. COMMUNICATION TREE > 8.1 Internal Communications
chunks.text: On declaration of an SBD, the Plan owner notifies the Management Committee and the department heads through the Adviser's mass notification application, followed by telephone. Each department head then contacts every member of his or her team. Every employee must acknowledge the notification within 30 minutes and confirm his or her location and ability to work. The BCP Coordinator tracks acknowledgments and follows up on any employee who has not responded.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated February 9, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. COMMUNICATION TREE > 8.2 Investors, Counterparties and Service Providers
chunks.text: The Head of Investor Relations, Celia Brandvold, coordinates communications with investors, in consultation with the Plan owner and the Chief Compliance Officer, and with the Administrator where investor dealing may be affected. The Head of Trading notifies the prime brokers and executing brokers of any change in trading locations or authorized contacts. The Chief Financial Officer notifies the Administrator of any expected delay in pricing or reconciliation.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated February 9, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 8. COMMUNICATION TREE > 8.3 Regulators
chunks.text: The Chief Compliance Officer determines whether any notice to the SEC, the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority or any other regulator is required and makes any required notice.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated February 9, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 9. PANDEMIC AND CYBER INCIDENT RESPONSE > 9.1 Pandemic Response
chunks.text: The Plan owner may activate the following phases in response to a public health emergency. In Phase 1 (monitoring), the Adviser reviews public health guidance, restricts non-essential travel and confirms remote access for all employees. In Phase 2 (split operations), the Adviser divides critical functions into two teams that do not occupy the office on the same days, and the Head of Trading and the execution trader work from separate locations at all times. In Phase 3 (full remote), the office is closed and all employees work remotely or from the alternate site. The Plan owner determines the timing of any return to the office.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated February 9, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 9. PANDEMIC AND CYBER INCIDENT RESPONSE > 9.2 Cyber Incident Response
chunks.text: The Incident Response Team is led by the Director of Technology, acting as Information Security Officer, and includes the Chief Compliance Officer, the President and Chief Operating Officer, a representative of the IT managed service provider and, as needed, outside counsel and a forensic investigation firm. On detection of a suspected incident, the Incident Response Team classifies its severity, contains the incident by isolating affected systems and disabling compromised credentials, preserves evidence, and eradicates the threat before systems are restored from clean backups. The Chief Compliance Officer determines whether notification is required to investors, affected individuals, regulators or law enforcement, and any notification to affected individuals is made within the deadlines set out in Section 12.3 of the Compliance Manual. The President and Chief Operating Officer notifies the carrier under the Adviser's cyber liability insurance policy. After each incident, the Incident Response Team documents the root cause and remediation and reports to the Management Committee.

chunks.label: Business Continuity Plan, dated February 9, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 9. PANDEMIC AND CYBER INCIDENT RESPONSE > 9.3 Temporary Delegation of Trading Authority
chunks.text: If the Chief Investment Officer is unable to perform his duties during an SBD, the Head of Risk and the most senior sector analyst available may jointly authorize trades necessary to reduce risk, meet margin calls or maintain compliance with the portfolio guidelines, but may not initiate new positions. The delegation ends when the Chief Investment Officer resumes his duties or the Management Committee determines otherwise.

chunks.label: Fee Schedule, dated January 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 1. SCOPE > 1.1 Application
chunks.text: This Fee Schedule sets out the management fees, incentive allocation, carried interest, minimum investments and redemption charges applicable to Sallowmere Partners Fund, LP (the "Flagship Fund"), Sallowmere Partners Offshore Fund, Ltd. (the "Offshore Fund") and Sallowmere Co-Investment Fund I, LP (the "Co-Investment Fund"). It summarizes the Offering Documents of each Fund, which control in the event of any inconsistency. chunks.label: Fee Schedule, dated January 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. MANAGEMENT FEES > 2.1 Rates by Class

chunks.label: Fee Schedule, dated January 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. MANAGEMENT FEES > 2.2 Large Investor Rate
chunks.text: The Large Investor Rate applies to the entire Class A capital account of an investor whose aggregate capital in the Flagship Fund and the Offshore Fund, together with the capital of its affiliates, is $50 million or more as of the first day of a calendar quarter. Eligibility is determined by the Administrator at the start of each quarter, and an investor that falls below the threshold as a result of redemptions reverts to the standard Class A rate from the following quarter. Market depreciation alone does not cause an investor to lose the Large Investor Rate.

chunks.label: Fee Schedule, dated January 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. MANAGEMENT FEES > 2.3 Billing Frequency and Basis
chunks.text: Management fees are calculated and payable quarterly in advance as of the first business day of each calendar quarter, based on each capital account (or each Offshore Fund shareholder's look-through share) as of that date, before accrual of any incentive allocation. Fees are charged once, at the Flagship Fund level, and the Offshore Fund pays no separate management fee.

chunks.label: Fee Schedule, dated January 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. MANAGEMENT FEES > 2.4 Proration
chunks.text: Subscriptions are accepted monthly. A subscription accepted as of the first day of a month other than the first month of a quarter bears a management fee pro-rated for the remaining months of that quarter, payable on the subscription date.

chunks.label: Fee Schedule, dated January 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. INCENTIVE ALLOCATION > 3.1 Rate
chunks.text: The general partner of the Flagship Fund receives an incentive allocation equal to 20% of the net profits allocated to each Class A capital account and 15% of the net profits allocated to each Class F capital account. Class E capital accounts bear no incentive allocation.

chunks.label: Fee Schedule, dated January 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 3. INCENTIVE ALLOCATION > 3.2 High Water Mark and Timing
chunks.text: The incentive allocation is subject to a high water mark with a loss carryforward, and there is no hurdle rate. It is determined as of December 31 of each year and as of the effective date of any redemption.

chunks.label: Fee Schedule, dated January 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. CO-INVESTMENT FUND > 4.1 Management Fee
chunks.text: The Co-Investment Fund pays no management fee.

chunks.label: Fee Schedule, dated January 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. CO-INVESTMENT FUND > 4.2 Carried Interest
chunks.text: The general partner of the Co-Investment Fund receives carried interest equal to 10% of net realized profits, distributed only after investors have received distributions equal to 100% of their capital contributions and their share of expenses. No carried interest is paid on unrealized gains.

chunks.label: Fee Schedule, dated January 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 4. CO-INVESTMENT FUND > 4.3 Expenses
chunks.text: The Co-Investment Fund bears its administration, audit, tax and legal expenses. Organizational expenses were borne by the Co-Investment Fund up to $150,000, with any excess borne by the Adviser.

chunks.label: Fee Schedule, dated January 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. REDEMPTIONS, TERMINATION AND REFUNDS > 5.1 Redemption Terms
chunks.text: Interests in the Flagship Fund and shares of the Offshore Fund may be redeemed as of the last business day of any calendar quarter on at least 65 days' prior written notice. Each Fund may limit aggregate redemptions as of any quarter-end to 20% of its net asset value. Ninety percent of redemption proceeds are ordinarily paid within 30 days after the redemption date, and a holdback of 10% applies to a full redemption until completion of the annual audit. Investors in the Co-Investment Fund have no redemption rights.

chunks.label: Fee Schedule, dated January 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. REDEMPTIONS, TERMINATION AND REFUNDS > 5.2 Early Redemption Fee
chunks.text: A redemption effective within 12 months after an investor's initial subscription is subject to an early redemption fee of 3% of the amount redeemed. The fee is retained by the Fund for the benefit of remaining investors and is not paid to the Adviser. The fee does not apply to Class E interests.

chunks.label: Fee Schedule, dated January 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. REDEMPTIONS, TERMINATION AND REFUNDS > 5.3 Termination of Investment Management Agreements
chunks.text: Each investment management agreement between the Adviser and a Fund may be terminated by either party on 90 days' prior written notice.

chunks.label: Fee Schedule, dated January 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 5. REDEMPTIONS, TERMINATION AND REFUNDS > 5.4 Refunds
chunks.text: If an investment management agreement terminates during a quarter, or if the general partner permits a redemption as of a date other than a quarter-end, the unearned portion of the prepaid management fee is refunded pro rata within 30 days.

chunks.label: Fee Schedule, dated January 1, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 6. MINIMUM INVESTMENTS > 6.1 Minimums
chunks.text: The minimum initial investment in each of the Flagship Fund and the Offshore Fund is $1,000,000, and the minimum additional investment is $250,000. The minimum commitment to the Co-Investment Fund was $5,000,000. The general partner of each Fund, or the board of directors of the Offshore Fund, may accept lesser amounts in its discretion.

chunks.label: Memorandum: Amendments to Firm Policies and Fee Schedule, dated August 24, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. AMENDMENTS > 2.1 Compliance Manual Section 4.5 (Minimum Holding Period)
chunks.text: The minimum holding period in Section 4.5 of the Compliance Manual is extended from 30 calendar days to 60 calendar days. Access persons must hold any position in a reportable security acquired in a covered account for at least 60 calendar days from the date of acquisition, and may not close a short position within 60 calendar days of opening it. Positions acquired before September 1, 2026 remain subject to the 30-day period. The disgorgement and hardship exception provisions of Section 4.5 are unchanged. This amendment supersedes Section 4.5 of the Compliance Manual.

chunks.label: Memorandum: Amendments to Firm Policies and Fee Schedule, dated August 24, 2026
chunks.section: SECTION 2. AMENDMENTS > 2.2 Compliance Manual Section 4.6 (Quarterly Transaction Reports)
chunks.text: Quarterly transaction reports must be submitted within 15 calendar days after the end of each calendar quarter, rather than within 30 calendar days. The first report subject to the new deadline is the report for the quarter ending September 30, 2026, which is due by October 15, 2026. The deadlines for initial and annual holdings reports are unchanged. This amendment supersedes the quarterly reporting deadline in Section 4.6 of the Compliance Manual.

chunks.label: Memorandum: Amendments to Firm Policies and Fee Schedule, dated August 24, 2026

chunks.text: The limit on gifts that supervised persons may accept from any person or entity that does business or seeks to do business with the Adviser or the Funds is reduced from $250 to $100 per source per calendar year. Gifts received on or after September 1, 2026 count against the reduced limit together with gifts received from the same source earlier in 2026. The limits on gifts given in Section 5.3 and on business entertainment in Section 5.4 are unchanged. This amendment supersedes Section 5.2 of the Compliance Manual.

This amendment supersedes Section 2.3 of the Valuation Policy.
